• The average length of the growing season in the contiguous 48 states has increased by more than two weeks since the beginning of the 20th A particularly large and steady increase has occurred since the 1970s. The length of the growing season has increased in almost every state, with the most dramatic increases in the West and the least in the Southeast.
  • Growing season length is expected to continue to increase by the end of this century under all emissions scenarios. All states are projected to experience increases.
  • Higher emissions scenarios are expected to lead to larger increases in length of growing season. Under the high and very high emissions scenarios, some states could have an extra two months or more by the end of this century, compared with current growing conditions.
